changelog:
What you'll see with this update:
• Update reliability: files now come from a version-pinned source, so an update can never half-install again (a unit could previously show the new version while still running old settings, and then refuse to re-apply).
• 'Config Check' row: the result shows just ok / restored / error / waiting -- no trailing number (it was an internal timestamp).
• The settings row 'Boots' is now 'Warnings' (in future it can carry alerts other than booting, too): it reads 'Repeated restarts' instead of the cryptic 'RESTART_STORM', with a plain-English message ('The unit restarted N times in the last 24h... please contact Cytech Support.'). The guard itself is unchanged: it flags 5+ restarts in 24h so Cytech can help.
• Config self-healing: if the main settings file is ever damaged, the unit repairs it from the last known-good copy (at boot, or within 4 hours while running) and tells you (popup + email).
• A 'Config Check' row in the settings screen, refreshed right after every restart and every 4 hours.
• A clean alert-email setup: your address field is 'My Email for Alerts'; Register shows its result on screen; alerts always reach Cytech Support too, with your address copied automatically.
details:
v43 is the fleet-wide release. Its content was developed as the v42 series (v42 plus the fix-revisions 42a-42f, which only ever ran on the bench unit); 42a was an early rename-only attempt and 42d was a same-content re-ship for a delivery problem, so neither appears as a change below. What ships:
(1) CDN-proof downloads. raw.githubusercontent.com serves each URL from a CDN with max-age=300, keyed by the URL itself (a query string does NOT create a separate entry -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device downloading right after a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with no error, then write the new version label -- silently half-updated, and permanently unable to re-apply ('the units can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date'). The bench unit hit exactly that during the 42c release. THE FIX: every release is git-tagged with its version (43) and files are downloaded from the tag URL -- a URL no device has ever fetched, so it can never be served from cache. The manifest itself stays on the branch URL (stale reads there are harmless: 'up to date' for at most 5 minutes, then the next check is fresh). .cytech_secrets.example documents that CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL must not be pinned to a tag (the tag changes every release).
(2) cytech_integrity_check.py writes the status word only ('ok'), not 'ok <epoch>' -- the epoch leaked onto the Config Check dashboard row as an unexplained number.
(3) The boot guard state RESTART_STORM became REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain-English messages ('Repeated restarts detected' popup/email; message 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.'). Automation id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3b) The sensor 'Cytech Boot Status' is renamed 'Cytech Warning' -- the row is expected to carry other warnings besides boot/restart ones -- and its unique_id is bumped to cytech_warning_result_sensor on purpose: the entity registry pins an entity_id at first registration, so a name change alone would NOT move the id. A bumped unique_id re-registers every unit fresh as sensor.cytech_warning; units that already ran v35+ keep the orphaned sensor.cytech_boot_status (unreferenced, harmless). The on-disk result file (/config/.cytech_boot_result) and the dashboard row's message attribute are unchanged.
(4) The runtime integrity check also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), not just every 4 hours, so the Config Check row shows its real result within minutes instead of 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart; before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'.
(5) Config self-healing: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check -- at boot and every 4 hours while running), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts (runtime corruption is repaired the same day it happens, before the next update's restart could land the system in HA recovery mode), and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v43 also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
